videos.script: This lesson is about the parts of a page that are not prose. {{table}} First, tables. The bookshop's opening hours are a table: days down the side, times across the top. A table is for that kind of data, where every value has a row and a column. It is not for laying out a page, and the lesson says why. {{alt}} Then pictures. A picture on a page needs words. Somebody who cannot see it, or whose connection did not load it, gets the words instead. Writing those words well is a skill, and the lesson gives you the rules. {{shift}} Next, a problem you have met as a reader. You start reading, a picture arrives, and the text jumps down the screen. Two attributes stop that, and you will watch the jump measured, before and after. {{srcset}} A phone does not need the picture a large monitor needs. HTML can offer several files and let the browser choose. You will see which file Chromium picked at five sizes, and why. {{lazy}} Then pictures far down the page, which can wait until somebody scrolls near them. {{video}} And at the end, video and audio, with the one thing every recording needs: captions. {{end}}
